literalCorrections.rule:
Three independent bugs in the cell-text extractor produced every literal in `corrections`. (1) NBSP: Confluence authors press Ctrl+Shift+Space inside spans to stop identifiers wrapping, so the page carries U+00A0 MID-TOKEN ($XDSDocumentEntry\u00a0ClassCode, 14d4debf-8f97-4251-9a74\u00a0-a90016b0af0d). The extractor maps every whitespace character, NBSP included, to U+0020. NBSP must NOT be treated as whitespace inside an identifier cell: in an identifier context it is deleted, in prose it becomes a space. Verified: 0 of the 243,245 strings in spec-build still contain U+00A0, which is exactly the symptom - the information that it was an NBSP was destroyed at parse time. (2) footnotes: page 54788213 carries all 10 digit markers in the corpus. The extractor flattens the cell with a text join, so $XDSDocumentEntry ClassCode 1 becomes "$XDSDocumentEntry ClassCode 1". Strip whose text is a bare 1-2 digit run BEFORE flattening. On six rows the author typed the marker INSIDE the (CreationTimeFrom5, ServiceStartTimeTo\u00a0\u00a06, Status\u00a0\u00a03), so a second, guarded pass is needed: strip a trailing 1-2 digit run from an identifier only when the page has a numbered footnote list, the digit indexes into it, and the de-suffixed form is corroborated (a golden sample, or another row on another page). Footnotes 5 and 6 on that page literally name "CreationTimeFrom and CreationTimeTo" and "ServiceStartTimeFrom, ServiceStartTimeTo, ServiceStopTimeFrom and ServiceStopTimeTo" without digits - that is the corroboration. (3) Block-level joins:

,

and
boundaries inside one are joined with a single space, which merges two element paths into one unusable string (./extension/url= ”...” ./extension/valueReference) and leaves a space after "url=". Block boundaries must become newlines; only INLINE markup (, , , , ) is unwrapped with no separator at all. Prefer the descendant: in every identifier column on these pages the identifier is exactly the element text, and taking it first sidesteps the sibling entirely.

openQuestions.question: Page 7766254 states only that the response is signed 'Sign the Assertion way' and hands the job to an external tool (https://www.samltool.com/sign_response.php). No ds:Signature internals are specified anywhere: no canonicalization method, digest method, signature method, transform list, reference URI convention, KeyInfo/X509Data requirement, and no statement of where inside the Assertion the element sits.
openQuestions.why: The ds:Signature member records ONLY that a signature exists and that it covers the Assertion. Its children are deliberately empty. A checker must not report a signature's internals as conforming or non-conforming against this structure.

openQuestions.question: The page lists exactly ONE signing option — 'Sign the Assertion way' — as a single bullet under the plural phrase 'A SAML Response can be signed in:'. The plural wording suggests a second option (Response-level signing) was intended and is missing from the page.
openQuestions.why: Only Assertion-level signing is modelled. Response-level signing is neither required nor forbidden here.

openQuestions.question: Page 7766237 states 'Organization ID = National Organization OID', but the skeleton's sample value is '10000300236625' — a 14-digit number, not a dotted OID. spec-build/constants.json records NPHIES national organization identifiers in the same flat-numeric shape.
openQuestions.why: No format rule is asserted for Organization ID. A checker must not require a dotted OID here, and must not require a 14-digit number either.

openQuestions.question: That 'Provider ID' is carried in saml:Subject/saml:NameID is inferred from the page's colour coding (the variable legend colours 'Provider ID' blue, and 1095650865 in the NameID is the only blue-highlighted value).
